A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation, the AVISeg benchmark, and AVISM. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original AVISeg benchmark evaluations, reproduced zero-shot comparisons, ablation results, and qualitative analyses in Section 6 and the supplement.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds a similarity-loss ablation and weight sensitivity study in Appendix D, Table 7.

M1.justification: AVISM retains the same encoders, frame-level localizer, video-level tracker, fusion modules, and training objectives. The similarity loss and its default weight of 0.5 already appear in v2 Section 5.4; v4 adds evaluation of this existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 926-video AVISeg benchmark, 26 categories, four domains, and silent/single-source/multiple-source scenarios. The pretraining datasets remain represented. Section 4 expands source citations without establishing a change in the underlying data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain the same supervised and zero-shot comparator sets, including VITA, AVSegFormer, COMBO, Sam4AVS, BuboGPT, PG-Video-LLaVA, and AL-Ref-SAM 2. The appendix retains their evaluation adaptations and qualitative comparisons. Newly cited related work is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 7 introduces similarity-loss removal and weight settings of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0; Table 6 drops the Swin-L ImageNet-only configuration. Algorithm 1 also revises documented FSLA checking logic. Shared data splits and training settings remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish reruns of the retained results.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly tests the contribution of similarity loss and sensitivity to its weight. Removing the Swin-L ImageNet-only row from Table 6 reduces the evidence isolating COCO pretraining for that backbone. Other fusion, window-size, backbone, qualitative, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The new ablation follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds FSLA/HOTA/mAP results of 32.71/52.45/35.77 without similarity loss, 38.97/59.92/38.22 at weight 0.1, and 42.08/61.63/40.49 at weight 1.0. Its default-weight result repeats 42.78/61.73/40.57. Table 6 removes the Swin-L ImageNet-only result, 49.15/68.81/49.06. Shared numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds explicit category-equality conditions for single- and multiple-source frames and a matching condition for single-source evaluation. These revise the formal pseudocode beyond notation changes and bring it closer to the existing prose criterion. The task definition and other mathematical formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing AVIS and AVISeg/FSLA, proposing AVISM, outperforming related methods, and exposing multimodal large models' instance-localization and temporal limitations. The additional ablation supports an existing contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes degradation without similarity loss to poor token/query association, feature misalignment, identity switches, and tracking failures, especially among same-category instances. Existing interpretations of the main results, failure conditions, and future-work limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit dataset/code availability statement and project repository link in the abstract, absent from v2, and expands dataset-source attribution in Section 4. Core implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and multimodal-model prompts remain unchanged after matching relocated content.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the ECMVAE discussion with CAVP and its construction of paired audio-image data using COCO and VGGSound. V4 also adds introductory audio-visual research citations and additional AVQA references in Section 4. The overall research positioning remains stable; publication updates and duplicate-reference consolidation do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized wording edits, updates author/affiliation information, and adds acknowledgments. It moves the metric-motivation paragraph into Appendix B, changes supplementary numbering to A-H, and places future-work discussion before the qualitative figure pages. Most exposition and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 7 and shortens Table 6, redraws Figure 2(e) with clearer labeling and contrast, color-codes Figure 4, and adds section references to Figures 3 and 6. Tables and appendix figures are repositioned, while the qualitative examples remain unchanged. These are localized display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly strengthens support for the existing similarity loss and default weight through Table 7, improves agreement between FSLA pseudocode and its stated category criterion, and adds code/data access information and clearer diagrams. These gains outweigh the limited loss of pretraining evidence from deleting the Swin-L ImageNet-only control in Table 6. The main findings and contributions remain unchanged.
